paras: Welcome to St. Augustine, the city which the Spanish founded in 1565. It is often called the oldest city in the United States, and it is full of places that tell its long story. I am Rosa, the guide who will walk with you today.

Our first stop is the Castillo de San Marcos, a fort which the Spanish built more than three centuries ago. Its walls are made of coquina, a stone that is made of tiny shells. When cannonballs hit the walls, they did not break them. They sank into the soft stone, and the fort is still standing today.

Next, we walk down St. George Street, where there are no cars, only people, shops and old wooden houses. Then we visit Flagler College. It was a luxury hotel which Henry Flagler opened in 1888. Today, the students who study there eat in a dining hall with seventy-nine Tiffany glass windows.

Our last stop is the lighthouse, which was finished in 1874. The people who climb to the top can see the ocean and the whole historic city. And at night, guides who love a good story take visitors on ghost tours. Are the ghosts real? That is a question that every visitor answers alone.

items.situation: Tell me about a person who is important in your life, in one sentence.
tips: My mother is the person who taught me to cook.

items.situation: Describe your house in Brazil with where.
tips: It is the house where I grew up.

items.situation: Describe a song that you love, with which or that.
tips: Livin' on a Prayer is a song which I know by heart.

items.situation: Correct me: 'The doctor which helped me was Brazilian.'
tips: The doctor who helped me was Brazilian.
A doctor is a person: who.

items.situation: Join these two sentences: 'This is the beach. I walk my dogs there.'
tips: This is the beach where I walk my dogs.
One sentence, and no 'there' at the end.

listenings.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the ghost tour. My name is Jack, and I am the guide who will take you through the dark streets tonight. We start here, at the old city gates, which are more than two hundred years old. Look at the small house next to the gates. A young woman called Elizabeth lived there, a long time ago. People say she waited every night for a man who never came back. Today, some visitors say they see a light in the window, like a candle. Is it Elizabeth? I do not know. Stay close to me, and let's walk to the next house, where the story is even stranger.

Hello, and welcome to the St. Augustine Lighthouse. I am a volunteer here, and I love this place. The tower which you see today was finished in 1874. There are two hundred and nineteen steps to the top, so take your time, and drink some water first. The keepers, who took care of the light, lived with their families in the house next to the tower. Today, that house is a museum where you can see how they lived. From the top, you can see the ocean, the beaches and the whole historic city. Enjoy the climb!

extra_audio.text: Our tour starts at the city gates, where we meet our guide. Then we visit the fort which the Spanish built. After that, we walk down the street where there are no cars. Next, we see the hotel which Henry Flagler opened in 1888. Finally, we climb the lighthouse that has two hundred and nineteen steps.
